title: Know What Every Bot on Your Team Did
summary: Keep one daily record of what each bot bought, posted, emailed or signed in to, with the rules you approved, so you can spot mistakes and risky requests early.

money_potential.label: Low
money_potential.basis: Assumes you run several bots that can buy, post or sign in; the value is checking time saved and problems caught early.
money_potential.note: Value tiers are our rough estimates (labelled Estimate) of relative value to the business, each with its assumption. They are not promises, income claims or advice. Results depend on your market, offer and effort.

how_it_makes_money: Mistakes and odd purchases get caught in days, not at the end of the month.
Less time digging through each bot to find out what happened.
who_its_for: Owners running several bots for their business.
Teams that share bots between people.

stack.name: Security Agent
stack.role: Gives each bot an ID, keeps the rules you approve and logs outside activity, purchases and red flags every day.
stack.creator: JennyMarquis

stack.name: Chief of Staff (Aryaman)
stack.role: Surfaces only the decisions that need you, so the security record does not get lost in your inbox.
stack.creator: aryamankhawow

steps.name: Security Agent
steps.does: Keeps one record of activity and red flags

steps.name: You
steps.does: Approve, block or change a rule

steps: Approve a short list of safety rules and red flags.
Have each active bot send a daily log.
Review the record weekly and tighten rules where needed.
guardrails: Log counts and times, not message contents, unless you truly need them.
A log is not a lock: keep approval steps on purchases, sends and deletions.
